atoms.text: This guide configures Meridian Replicator to copy new objects from the bucket orders-primary in region north-1 to the bucket orders-dr in region south-2 for disaster recovery. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and neither bucket policy is changed. Create an IAM role named meridian-replicator-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal meridian-replicator.svc to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on orders-primary and its objects, so the service can list and read the source object versions. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject on orders-dr/* so that the replicated copies can be written to the destination. Enable versioning on both buckets, because replication tracks object versions. In the replication configuration of orders-primary, set the replication role to the identifier of meridian-replicator-role and limit the rule to the prefix invoices/. Upload a test object under invoices/ and confirm that it appears in orders-dr with a replication status of COMPLETE.

This guide configures Meridian Replicator to copy new objects from the bucket orders-primary in region north-1 to the bucket orders-dr in region south-2 for disaster recovery. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of orders-primary whose Principal is the service principal meridian-replicator.svc and which allows storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on the bucket and its objects, so the service can list and read the source object versions. Add a statement to the bucket policy of orders-dr that names the same service principal and allows storage:PutObject on orders-dr/*, so that the replicated copies can be written to the destination. Enable versioning on both buckets, because replication tracks object versions. In the replication configuration of orders-primary, identify the service principal as the replicating party and limit the rule to the prefix invoices/. Upload a test object under invoices/ and confirm that it appears in orders-dr with a replication status of COMPLETE.

This guide allows Vaultline Backup to write nightly database snapshot exports to the bucket db-snapshots-prod under the prefix nightly/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy of db-snapshots-prod stays unchanged. Create an IAM role named vaultline-backup-role and set its trust policy to permit the service principal vaultline-backup.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on db-snapshots-prod/nightly/*, because large snapshots are uploaded in parts. Also allow storage:GetBucketLocation and storage:ListBucket on the bucket so the service can check existing snapshot names before it writes. Configure the Vaultline job with the role identifier and set the destination to db-snapshots-prod/nightly/. Add a lifecycle rule on the bucket that expires objects under nightly/ after 30 days. Run a manual job and verify that a snapshot object with the current date in its key appears in the bucket.

This guide allows Vaultline Backup to write nightly database snapshot exports to the bucket db-snapshots-prod under the prefix nightly/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of db-snapshots-prod whose Principal is the service principal vaultline-backup.svc. In that statement, allow storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on db-snapshots-prod/nightly/*, because large snapshots are uploaded in parts. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows storage:GetBucketLocation and storage:ListBucket on the bucket so the service can check existing snapshot names before it writes. Configure the Vaultline job to use its own service identity and set the destination to db-snapshots-prod/nightly/. Add a lifecycle rule on the bucket that expires objects under nightly/ after 30 days. Run a manual job and verify that a snapshot object with the current date in its key appears in the bucket.

This guide sets up Argent Sync to copy audit log files from the bucket logs-primary to the bucket compliance-vault, which has object lock enabled with a 365-day retention period. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policies are not edited. Create an IAM role named argent-sync-role whose trust policy allows the service principal argent-sync.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on logs-primary and its objects for reading the log files. Allow storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectRetention on compliance-vault/audit/* in the same policy so each copy is written with its retention setting. Set the role identifier in the Argent Sync pipeline and schedule the copy every 15 minutes for the prefix audit/. The service writes each object once and never overwrites or deletes existing copies. Check a copied object's retention metadata to confirm that the retain-until date is 365 days ahead.

This guide gives Stratus Snapshot Manager the ability to store weekly virtual machine image exports in the bucket vm-archive, using one prefix per machine ID. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the vm-archive bucket policy is not modified. Create an IAM role named stratus-snapshot-role and add a trust policy that lets the service principal stratus-snapshot.svc assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on vm-archive/images/*, since each export is several gigabytes and is uploaded in parts. Add storage:GetObject on the same resource so that the service can read each export back and compare its checksum after the upload. Reference the role identifier in the export schedule and set the target to vm-archive/images/{machine-id}/. Add a lifecycle rule that moves objects under images/ to the archive storage class after 14 days. Run one export and confirm that the checksum comparison step reports a match.

This guide configures Parallax Mirror to replicate media assets, including their object tags, from the bucket media-origin to the bucket media-dr in a separate region. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and no bucket policy is changed. Create an IAM role named parallax-mirror-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal parallax-mirror.svc to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:ListBucket, storage:GetObject, and storage:GetObjectTagging on media-origin and its objects. The same policy allows storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectTagging on media-dr/*, so that tags are written together with each copied object. Select the role in the Parallax Mirror job and set it to replicate only new and changed objects under assets/. Configure the job so that deletions in the source are not propagated, which leaves removed objects in media-dr. Upload a tagged image to media-origin/assets/ and verify that media-dr holds the same object with identical tags.

This guide configures Parallax Mirror to replicate media assets, including their object tags, from the bucket media-origin to the bucket media-dr in a separate region. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of media-dr for the same principal that allows storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectTagging on media-dr/*, so that tags are written together with each copied object. Set the Parallax Mirror job to use its own service identity and to replicate only new and changed objects under assets/. Configure the job so that deletions in the source are not propagated, which leaves removed objects in media-dr. Upload a tagged image to media-origin/assets/ and verify that media-dr holds the same object with identical tags.

This guide connects Tessera Backup Agent to the bucket fileshare-backup so that it can store incremental backups of a network file share and read them back during restores. Each host writes under its own prefix, hosts/{hostname}/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy of fileshare-backup is left as it is. Create an IAM role named tessera-agent-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal tessera-agent.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on fileshare-backup/hosts/*, which covers both the backup writes and the restore reads. Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting the listing prefix to hosts/. Enter the role identifier in the agent's configuration and set the repository path to fileshare-backup/hosts/{hostname}/. Run an initial full backup, then a second run, and check that the second run uploads only changed files.

This guide lets Halyard Restore store hourly cluster state snapshots in the versioned bucket cluster-state-backups and prune old snapshot versions. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create an IAM role named halyard-restore-role and configure its trust policy so that the service principal halyard-restore.svc can assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:PutObject on cluster-state-backups/etcd/* for writing each snapshot. Allow storage:ListBucketVersions on the bucket and storage:DeleteObjectVersion on cluster-state-backups/etcd/* so the service can remove versions beyond the newest 48. Set the role identifier in the Halyard Restore policy and the destination key to etcd/cluster-state.snap. Enable versioning on the bucket before the first run, because each hourly write creates a new version of the same key. After three runs, list the object versions and confirm that all three are present.

This guide configures Cobalt Copy to run a weekly one-way batch copy of machine learning datasets from the bucket datasets-prod to the bucket datasets-dr. The job reads objects from the source and writes them to the destination only when their checksums differ. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and neither bucket policy is modified. Create an IAM role named cobalt-copy-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal cobalt-copy.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on datasets-prod and its objects, so the job can enumerate keys and read the data. Allow storage:ListBucket on datasets-dr and storage:PutObject on datasets-dr/* in the same policy so that the job can compare existing keys and write the changed files. Specify the role identifier in the job definition and schedule it for Sunday at 02:00 UTC. The role has no delete permission on either bucket, so removed source files remain in datasets-dr. After the first run, compare object counts under the prefix training/ in both buckets.

This guide configures Cobalt Copy to run a weekly one-way batch copy of machine learning datasets from the bucket datasets-prod to the bucket datasets-dr. The job reads objects from the source and writes them to the destination only when their checksums differ. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of datasets-prod that names the service principal cobalt-copy.svc and allows storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on the bucket and its objects, so the job can enumerate keys and read the data. Add a statement to the bucket policy of datasets-dr for the same principal that allows storage:ListBucket on the bucket and storage:PutObject on datasets-dr/*, so that the job can compare existing keys and write the changed files. Configure the job definition to use the service's own identity and schedule it for Sunday at 02:00 UTC. Neither policy grants delete permission, so removed source files remain in datasets-dr. After the first run, compare object counts under the prefix training/ in both buckets.
